Tamaulipas education officials gathered in Nuevo Laredo on Friday for the fourth regional meeting of upper-secondary school academies, a working session aimed at strengthening teaching quality and improving student achievement, according to Sentido Común.

The meeting took place at COBAT plantel 01 in Nuevo Laredo, bringing together teachers from different upper-secondary subsystems across the region.

Igor Crespo Solís, subsecretary of Upper Secondary and Higher Education, presided over the session on behalf of Tamaulipas Education Secretary Miguel Ángel Valdez García. He described the academies as spaces for dialogue, reflection and collective work, saying that when teachers share experiences, knowledge, strategies and best practices, they enrich their work and create better learning opportunities for students.

During the session, teachers reviewed the results of the EXADIEMS diagnostic exam for upper-secondary students, identified priority learning areas and shared teaching strategies to address the main difficulties found in schools.

Crespo Solís said one of the main challenges in upper-secondary education is keeping teachers trained and up to date, particularly in the common curricular framework for upper-secondary education (MCCEMS) and the principles of the Nueva Escuela Mexicana. He added that today’s students face a world shaped by technology, artificial intelligence and a changing job market, making critical thinking, creativity, values and adaptability essential skills to develop.

Among the education authorities taking part were Nuevo Laredo Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas; Olegario Muñiz Cura, the commissioner in charge of DGETI Tamaulipas; and Gil Marcelino Aguilar, director of Upper Secondary Education. Crespo Solís said the education sector has the backing of the state government led by Governor Américo Villarreal Anaya, who has made education a central axis of his administration.

Sources: Sentido Común, November 7, 2026.
